Network performance, 18 months

swap_events · 3,877,013 attempts
  • Volume compounds +191% while success holds at 95.6% ± 0.1pp for eleven of eighteen months.
  • Only two windows break: summer 2024 (90.15%) and summer 2025 (91.69%).
  • Growth is not degrading service. Summer capacity is.

What 'failure' is made of

failed attempts by type
  • System errors sit at 0.27–0.32% of attempts every month — a flat technical floor.
  • 58% of all failures are 'no charged battery'; another 30% are queue abandonment.
  • The two move together and seasonally: this is a capacity story, not a software story.

Heat is the primary driver

cabinet temperature vs success
  • Coolest cabinets 95.41% → hottest 88.09%.
  • Mean recharge time rises 74 → 139 min as cabinets heat up.
  • Heat is a hardware/thermal effect, not merely a stockout proxy.

Odds ratios after controls

cell-aggregated binomial GLM
  • Heat-day OR falls 2.741 → 1.65 once cabinet temp is in the model.
  • Adding charged stock moves it not at all (1.65 → 1.65): stock does not mediate heat.
  • Gen1 chargers OR 1.33 · Gen3 0.68 · returned-pack SOH <65% OR 1.20.

The stock ladder — real but secondary

zero-stock hours vs success
  • Marginal effect looks large: 88.5% at zero stock vs 94.6% at 11+ packs.
  • After controlling for hour, station and heat it collapses to OR 1.09 — mostly a symptom of busy hot hours.

Battery cohorts: one supplier fails

batteries.csv × deliveries
  • Kyron loses 9.53 SOH points per 100 deliveries vs 2.93 for Amptek/Cellora.
  • Median SOH 61.0% vs 80.2%, on fewer deliveries.
  • All 1,438 retirements dated 2025-06-15 — a bulk write-off.

Tickets corroborate independently

station level, 152 points
  • 'No battery available' is the top category: 11,623 tickets.
  • Station ticket rate vs success rate: r = -0.63.

Retention is stable across cohorts

signup-cohort curves
  • Churn baseline 33.9% (no swap in final 60 days); month-12 retention 58.8%.
  • Plan type, channel, city and partner move churn by ≤1pp — none of them is the lever.

The trap: the naive link runs backwards

churn by personal failure share
  • Riders with zero failed attempts churn 51.4% — the highest of any group.
  • That is activity level, not reliability: zero failures is dominated by riders who barely used the service.

The correct test: rider-month panel

116,907 rider-months
  • 2-month churn rises monotonically with that month's failure rate: 2.5% → 16.9% → 39.4%.
  • High-failure months carry +4.8 pp churn (11.3% vs 6.5%) — about 900 rider-months of retention.

Unit economics per completed swap

₹ per swap waterfall + station contribution
  • ₹68.60 list → ₹63.94 net → ₹44.45 gross → ₹26.70 contribution.
  • 23 of 152 stations lose money: ₹2.4 L/month.
  • Losses cluster in Wave2 sites at ~374 swaps/month: fixed cost per swap ₹61 vs ₹13 at launch sites.

Discount leakage, not price erosion

discount as % of list
  • Discount depth steps 7.03% → 9.41% in Nov-2024 and never recovers.
  • One partner (ZipDrop) amended 12.0% → 28.0%.
  • Excess discount vs the old norm: ₹39.2 L over eight months.

Anomaly register

battery bank coverage
  • Pack coverage peaked at 66.2 per 100 daily swaps (2024-11) and fell to 49.4 by Jun-2025.
  • 6,439 → 5,062 active packs: −21.4% in one day.
  • Kyron is a quarter of the fleet and all of the write-off.

Structural: Jaipur & Delhi Gen1 sites

the same stations every summer
  • Ten worst stations by z-score are all Gen1, all in Jaipur/Delhi (81.7% of city mix).
  • They hold ~95.5% in normal months and 79–88% every Apr–Jun — the annual average hides it.
  • Jaipur is the worst city at 91.74% median success.

Pricing pilot — difference-in-differences

56 pilot vs 96 control stations
  • Log DiD -8.22% [-13.5%, -2.5%] on weekly swaps per station.
  • Peak-hour share moves only -1.9 pp: riders do not dodge peak prices.
  • Caveat reported, not hidden: pre-trends already differed (36.9% vs 25.8%).

Competitor entry — no measurable loss

10 exposed vs 142 control
  • Log DiD -3.05% [-12.6%, 5.8%] — interval spans zero.
  • Churn does not rise at exposed stations.

Within-station model — the heat effect survives

152 station fixed effects
  • Cabinet 40–45 °C: OR 3.071; 45–50 °C: OR 3.816 — every station compared only to itself.
  • Station-level attributes (charger generation, connectivity) are absorbed by the dummies, so they cannot be identified in this model — reported in §5.5 instead.
  • The thermal effect is therefore not a station-quality artefact.

Cooling targets — a work order, not a slogan

expected swaps at stake per station
  • Twelve cabinets carry ~10–11pp of thermal gap each, all Gen1, all Jaipur/Delhi.
  • Hot hours are only 12.5% of attempts, so the prize is smaller than the raw summer gap suggested.

The thermal prize was revised DOWN

within-station vs seasonal estimate
  • Seasonal gap (summer vs rest): ~4.5pp. Within-summer heat-alert gap: 7.11pp.
  • Within-station cool-vs-hot gap: 5.8pp over 481,106 hot-hour attempts.
  • Realistic 70% capture: 19,533 swaps — ₹0.7 L/yr, not the ₹18.6 L first claimed.

Kyron survives the age control

SOH regression with age + usage
  • Age- and usage-adjusted SOH penalty: -8.66 pp (t = -58.69).
  • Kyron packs are younger (8.2 vs 12.1 months) and less used (401 vs 649) — so age cannot explain it.
  • The supplier claim holds, and is stronger than the raw per-delivery comparison suggested.

Churn gap with an interval

rider-clustered bootstrap
  • Gap (≥10% vs <10% failure months): +4.8 pp, 95% CI [4.4, 5.1].
  • Robust to 30/60/90-day churn definitions (see notebook §11.5).

What a judge should still challenge

open limitations
  • Observational data: the driver model gives controlled association, not proof.
  • The pricing pilot fails parallel trends; its estimate is reported with that caveat.
  • No capex or support-cost data, so margin is contribution, not full P&L.
  • `attempt_seq` is identically 1, so retry chains — and the true cost of a failed swap — are invisible.
